blurb: Holomorphic functions, Cauchy's theorem, residues, conformal maps and the analytic continuation of ζ(s).

pics.alt: Lithograph portrait of the mathematician Augustin-Louis Cauchy
pics.caption: Augustin-Louis Cauchy (1789–1857), who founded complex function theory: his integral theorem (1825) and integral formula are the backbone of the subject.
pics.title: Augustin-Louis Cauchy 1901.jpg

pics.alt: Domain-colouring plot of the Riemann zeta function in the complex plane
pics.caption: A domain-colouring plot of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function ζ(s) for −40 ≤ Re s, Im s ≤ 40, with colour showing the argument of ζ(s). The colour cycles close up at the pole s = 1 and at the non-trivial zeros on the line Re s = 1/2, the first near Im s = ±14.13.
pics.title: Complex zeta.jpg
